notes: Baseline clean receipt. Solo meal at $48.20, well under the $75 domestic cap.

False-positive trap. Alcohol is present but fully compliant: documented client entertainment with 4 attendees (ALC-01 satisfied), $17 per attendee against the $30 cap (ALC-02 satisfied), $58.50 per person against the $75 cap (MEAL-01 satisfied). A system that flags on the presence of alcohol fails here.
Clean. Adapter is a peripheral well under the TECH-02 $200 ceiling.

Keyword trap, four ways. Beer-battered cod, an Arnold Palmer, a Spanish-language virgin mojito and rum cake all contain alcohol words and none is alcohol. Merchant name contains 'Tavern' but the MCC is 5812, not 5813. Any keyword matcher flags this receipt; a correct system passes it.
Large total but entirely compliant. Tests that amount alone does not drive a flag.
Threshold near-miss: $189 against the TECH-02 $200 per-item ceiling, so no pre-approval is required. Compare with RCP-026.

Cap near-miss: $53.00 per person against the $75 cap. Over $150 so MEAL-02 applies, and the attendee count is present, so it is satisfied. A team meal, which TIME-02 does not cover, so the absent trip record raises nothing.
Multilingual clean receipt. EUR 23 per person against the EUR 70 EMEA cap, and EUR 46 is below the EUR 50 VAT-documentation threshold in REG-04, so neither rule fires.
LAUNDRY-01 near-miss in the compliant direction: a 5-night trip clears the 4-night minimum. Compare with RCP-031.

expected_exceptions.reason: Alcohol on an individual meal with no attendee count and no entertainment context.

notes: The canonical alcohol violation. Total is under the meal cap, so ALC-01 is the only exception.

expected_exceptions.reason: Transaction at MCC 5921, a high-risk merchant category, raises an exception on its own.
Retail alcohol from an off-premise store is never reimbursable, regardless of business context.

notes: Two independent high exceptions. The attendee count and pre-approval reference are present and deliberately do not help: ALC-03 has no entertainment carve-out and EXC-02 states that a pre-approval waives only the rule that requires it.

expected_exceptions.reason: Headphones are personal electronics and are not reimbursable at any amount.
Submitted as Office Supplies; the contents are personal electronics.

review_signals.reason: MCC 5732 is medium risk and adds context, but is not an exception on its own.

notes: Misclassification is reported in addition to the item violation, per DOC-03. A system that reports only one of the two is incomplete.

expected_exceptions.reason: Gift cards and cash equivalents are never reimbursable at any amount.

notes: The greeting card is a restricted category but sits under the GIFT-01 $50 cap, so it raises nothing. Only the gift card is an exception.

expected_exceptions.reason: Cleaning and paper products are household goods and are not reimbursable.
Cooking wine purchased at a supermarket is retail alcohol.
Submitted as Office Supplies; the contents are groceries and household goods.

notes: Reverse keyword trap: cooking wine reads as an ingredient but is alcohol bought at retail, so ALC-03 applies and ALC-01 does not. Three exceptions on a $47.76 receipt, which also tests that severity rather than amount drives disposition.

expected_exceptions.reason: $214.80 per person against the $75 domestic daily cap.
$55.00 of alcohol per attendee against the $30 per-attendee cap.

notes: Alcohol is permitted here (ALC-01 satisfied by the attendee count) but breaches the per-attendee cap, so the correct exception is ALC-02 and not ALC-01. Distinguishing the two is the point of this receipt.

expected_exceptions.reason: Alcohol is never reimbursable for APAC-entity employees, overriding the entertainment allowance in ALC-01.

notes: Rule-precedence test. Under the global rules this receipt would pass: attendee count present (ALC-01), $5.40 alcohol per attendee (ALC-02), $21.78 per person against the APAC $60 cap (REG-02). The regional override is the only thing that makes it an exception, and a system that cites ALC-01 here has the right answer for the wrong reason.

expected_exceptions.reason: Transaction at MCC 7297, a high-risk merchant category.
Spa and massage services are personal care and are not reimbursable.
Submitted as Lodging; the contents are personal care services.

notes: A spa charge folded into a hotel stay. Tests that the MCC signal and the item signal are reported as separate exceptions rather than collapsed into one.

expected_exceptions.reason: Transaction at MCC 5944, a high-risk merchant category.
$180 against the $50 per-recipient cap for client gifts.

notes: The recipient is named, so the identifiability half of GIFT-01 is satisfied and only the cap is breached. A system that reports 'recipient not identifiable' has not read the line item.

expected_exceptions.reason: A tablet and its case are personal electronics and are not reimbursable.

notes: Japanese-language line items plus a JPY conversion. The case is written entirely in Japanese, and the tablet appears only under its product name, 'iPad Air', so catching both needs either the Japanese or knowledge of the product. The expense type is Computer Equipment and the items are personal electronics rather than peripherals, so TECH-01 applies and not TECH-02. DOC-03 does not apply: the policy lists personal electronics under Computer Equipment, so the declaration is correct even though the item is not reimbursable.

expected_exceptions.reason: Same employee, same merchant, same day as RCP-021. Each receipt sits below the $75 daily meal cap; the combined $145.50 exceeds it.

notes: Cross-receipt rule: this receipt is compliant in isolation and only becomes an exception when grouped with RCP-021. Per TIME-03, the split rule replaces the meal cap for the group, so MEAL-01 is not raised separately.

expected_exceptions.reason: Same employee, same merchant, same day as RCP-020. Each receipt sits below the $75 daily meal cap; the combined $145.50 exceeds it.

notes: The second half of the split pair. TIME-03 applies to every receipt in the group, so both RCP-020 and RCP-021 carry the exception.

expected_exceptions.reason: A lunch and a gift basket provided to a municipal procurement official are prohibited under the anti-corruption policy, at any amount.

notes: The only critical exception in the set, and it routes to Compliance rather than the audit queue. The amount is $45, below the GIFT-01 $50 cap, so the cap is deliberately not breached: what makes this critical is who received it — the lunch as well as the gift, since GIFT-04 covers meals too. A system driven only by thresholds sees nothing here.

expected_exceptions.reason: Receipt total of $186 exceeds the $75 itemization threshold and no itemization was provided.

notes: Non-itemized receipt. The per-person figure of $62 is within the cap and the attendee count satisfies MEAL-02, so DOC-01 is the only exception. The correct behaviour is to flag the absence of evidence, not to speculate about what was bought.

expected_exceptions.reason: Tobacco products are not reimbursable.

notes: A high exception hiding inside a $20.50 breakfast receipt. Tests that line-item analysis runs on small receipts, which is where most keyword systems stop looking.

expected_exceptions.reason: Two glasses of white wine on an individual meal with no attendee count.

notes: German-language alcohol with no English token to match. EUR 35 is below the EUR 50 VAT threshold in REG-04 and below the EMEA meal cap, so ALC-01 is the only exception.

expected_exceptions.reason: A single peripheral at $329 exceeds the $200 ceiling and no pre-approval reference is recorded.

notes: A monitor is an unrestricted category and still breaches policy on amount. Tests that the policy engine evaluates thresholds and approvals, not just restricted categories. The cable is under the ceiling and raises nothing. Compare with RCP-006.

expected_exceptions.reason: Clothing is not reimbursable and no baggage-delay reference is recorded on the expense.

notes: The baggage-delay carve-out in PERS-02 would permit this up to $150, but no delay reference is present, so the carve-out does not apply. A system that cites the carve-out to pass the receipt has inverted the burden of evidence.

review_signals.reason: MCC 5912 is medium risk and raises a review signal only.

notes: Nothing is wrong here: $14.48 of OTC medication on a trip, against the $25 HEALTH-01 allowance. The medium-risk MCC alone moves it to review, and reporting MCC-02 as an exception would be a false positive.

review_signals.reason: Local transaction time of 02:14 falls in the 00:00-05:00 overnight window.

notes: An overnight meal with unremarkable contents. The timing is worth sampling and is not evidence of anything on its own.

review_signals.reason: Travel-related expense type with no associated trip record.

notes: A travel meal with no trip attached, dated on a Saturday. TIME-02 is the expected signal. TIME-04 does not apply: it needs recorded trip dates, and with no trip record at all TIME-02 covers the case.

expected_exceptions.reason: Dry cleaning on a 2-night trip, below the 4-night minimum.

notes: One of two receipts (with RCP-032) where a single low-severity exception stands alone, so EXC-01 puts the receipt in review rather than flag. A system that flags this has not implemented the severity ladder. Compare with RCP-009, where the same item on a 5-night trip passes.

expected_exceptions.reason: Software subscription with no manager approval reference.

notes: A documentation gap rather than a spend violation. Low severity alone means review, not flag.
